findings.correction: Regenerate slice-overlay-drift-101.svg from an overlay payload whose x_points_ref is non-empty, or reword the caption so it names only nova's and imas-efit's X-point markers and states that the generating state is marked at its axis only.
findings.text: blocking: the overlay caption states 'the generating state's are open grey, a circle at its axis and a cross at its X-point', but the committed slice-overlay-drift-101.svg draws no such cross. The SVG carries exactly five marker glyphs, each used once (nova triangle and plus, imas-efit square and diamond, one open grey circle), and the payload the panel is drawn from has no generating-state saddle at all: the study's overlay npz holds x_points_ref with shape (0, 2), so paint.py:150 draws nothing for it while still drawing the grey axis circle at paint.py:142. The figure therefore omits the generating state's admitted X-point, which nova's binding figure rules require a panel comparing a solved field with its reference to draw for BOTH sets ('draws BOTH sets of nulls in their own styles, and says in the caption which is which'), and the caption asserts the reviewed marker instead. The repair is either to regenerate the panel with the generating state's saddle drawn (reference.py already computes and stores x_points, so this is plumbed) or to correct the caption to the two null sets the figure actually marks.

findings.correction: Say six tests were added, or list all six, so the citation's enumeration matches the delta it cites.
findings.text: non-blocking: the citation says '(the added tests are the call-site guard and its negative control, and the added duplicate-slice refusal of an arm)', which reads as an exhaustive account of the 16-to-22 delta, but six tests separate the base e28db604e (16) from the head b76c7d054 (22): test_current_draw_carries_the_sequence_colour_and_keeps_its_size, test_run_nova_records_a_current_draw_that_holds_the_sequence_memory, test_run_nova_guard_catches_a_white_current_draw, test_row_matched_arm_is_available_by_name, test_grouped_refuses_a_slice_one_arm_carries_twice and test_grouped_merges_shards_that_do_not_repeat_a_slice. A reader counting guards from this sentence undercounts them by half.

findings.correction: Compose the row-matched stem through a declared_stem variant that takes the row set as an argument (or assert the declared set is 'all' beside this line) instead of appending a literal '-loops'.
findings.text: non-blocking: row_matched composes the row-matched arm name as declared_stem('nova', sequence) + '-loops', which is correct only while DECLARED_ROWS['nova'] is 'all'. If nova's declared row set ever becomes 'loops', declared_stem already returns 'nova-<sequence>-200-0.0100-loops' and the appended suffix looks up '...-loops-loops', so the row-matched block would silently report the arm absent. The same commit removed two hand-spelled copies of the stem rule from figures.py, and this line re-spells the row-set suffix that declared_stem owns; the row-matched lookup wants a stem builder that takes the row set explicitly rather than a literal appended to the declared one.
